findings.reason: the section's own measure cannot pass against the code it cites, so a reader takes §3 as satisfied when the assertion it names was never made true.
findings.text: §3 is declared `done` (meta `plan-section-declarations`), but its done-when requires "a path appearing only in prose is charged at a reference cost … requiring the difference to be the reference cost and not the file size", and the shipped `_declared_input_files` (reckon/crew/routing.py:3026) charges a mention nothing at all — the authorising comment at html:256 states this outright ("a mention costs nothing"), and no `reference_tokens` is ever set for a mention in `_context_file_inputs`

findings.reason: a section claimed complete on a mechanism its cited rule explicitly declines to build cannot be closed or reviewed on one verdict; §4 must be un-done or its done-when rewritten to what "not preloaded without an opt-out" actually establishes.
findings.text: §4 is declared `done`, and its done-when requires "the opt-out is asserted to be recorded on the run" and "a path that is both opted out and declared as a write path is refused rather than silently resolved", but no anchor opt-out exists anywhere in the tree (grep for anchor/opt-out/no-preload over `reckon/crew/` returns no mechanism, and `TaskNode` carries no such field), which is why the same comment claims §4 is met "without any opt-out"

findings.reason: a section's behaviour was chosen in code without the decision that governs it being locked, so the plan records a settled section and an open decision on the same question.
findings.text: §3 is declared `done` while the decision that selects its behaviour, `reference-cost` (`flat` / `capped-head` / `zero`), still has an empty `data-choice`, and the code has in fact settled it at `zero`; §3's body at html:111 and 115 argues for a nonzero reference charge while the shipped behaviour is no charge

findings.reason: the section argues its case from a mechanism the code no longer has and measures a directory the code does not grant, so a node dispatched against it would test the wrong scope; §7's `done` status rests on the per-node grant, which is a different resolution from the one its body argues.
findings.text: §7 states that `_grant_landing_write_paths` "gives every dispatched node two shared repository paths — the cumulative evidence record and the plan file … so those belong to all of them", but the function's docstring (reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:794) says "The default scope is the node's fragment, so two nodes on one plan hold disjoint scopes", `_shared_landing_paths` (dispatch_claims.py:704) says the shared paths "are no longer granted by default", and the actual grant is `_landing_fragment_paths` returning `docs/figures/<plan>/<node.id>` plus the node's own evidence fragment — so §7's premise is false and its done-when (html:201) requires the parent `docs/figures/<plan>/` while the code grants the per-node child

findings.reason: two sections for one deliverable cannot each be closed on one verdict, and §8's gap claim would send a node to re-add a breakdown that already exists under another name.
findings.text: §8 delivers the same thing as §2 (report the per-file breakdown beside the total) and its supporting evidence ("the per-file term breakdown is not in the estimator — grep for `per_file`/`per-file` in `reckon/crew/routing.py` found none") is a name-based non-detection contradicted by the tree and by §2 itself: `_context_file_inputs` returns per-file records with `estimated_tokens` (routing.py:3153) and `_context_refusal_detail` already renders "largest contributing files" (routing.py:3425)
